en: The Therāpadāna: The Chapter on the Giver of a Support (Ālambaṇadāyakavagga) 7. The Apadāna of the Elder Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya I offered a golden ear-ornament to the Buddha, the supreme among men, who was seated beneath the Goatherd’s Banyan tree. Because of that deed, I have attained this state of being a monk; through the power of that gift, I have become one who possesses great splendor. Having performed that meritorious act, I have now reached the end of suffering. This is my final birth; there will be no further existence for me. This is my last body; I shall not take up another. I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra, which is difficult to traverse. I am now a sage who has attained the goal. I have reached the further shore of the ocean of existence. “While going out to the park grounds,
I saw the Leader of the World;
taking up a flower-ear ornament, I offered it to him.”
It was made of gold and well-crafted.
Having quickly ascended it,
I took my place upon the back of the elephant.
I offered it to Buddha Sikhin,
the Kinsman of the World.
Thirty-one eons ago,
The flower that I offered— of this flower-offering,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is its fruit.
In the twenty-seventh aeon from now,
I was once a lord of men known by the name Mahāpatāpa.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
It was in this way that the Venerable Elder Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya recited these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the Elder Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya.
